subject: Re: Sales discovery — model fit, evals, and regression concerns
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Tom Briggs <tom.briggs@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Diana Park <diana.park@acme-retail.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Jul 2026 14:02:00 -0000
Subject: Sales discovery — model fit & next steps

Hi Tom / Diana,

Great to meet you both on the demo earlier. Quick recap and clear next steps so we can keep the pilot moving: 

What we covered
- Primary goal: improve search-to-answer relevance for product pages (short-form responses and attribute extraction).
- Typical payload: 256 token prompts, avg 1.2 requests/sec per user, bursty daytime traffic.

Recommended initial model fit (based on today's sample prompts)- redwood-bert-2.3 (recommended for short-form extraction, best latency/cost balance)- open-gpt-13b-q4f (if you want higher-fidelity generation on long-form responses)

Artifacts attached
- eval_prompt_set_v1.jsonl (prompt set we used in the demo)
- benchmark links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-acme-benchmarks

Immediate next steps
1) I will share the full benchmark runs and recommended pin for pilot (target: redwood-bert-2.3).
2) Rishi (CS) will reach out to map success criteria and SLAs.
3) If you want, we can pin your pilot to a specific model version to prevent unexpected diffs during evaluation.

Can you confirm a good window next week for a short follow-up (20 min) to review the benchmark numbers?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

---
Note: attached prompt set is a trimmed export. For production evals we recommend adding a 500-sample holdout set for regression checks.
From: Tom Briggs <tom.briggs@acme-retail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Diana Park <diana.park@acme-retail.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Jul 2026 15:10:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Sales discovery — model fit & next steps

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the recap and the prompt set. Quick flag from our side: after your team’s platform pushed the latest default model update (v2.4) last week, we started seeing degraded output for some of our shortest prompts (examples attached).

What we observed
- Several short extraction prompts that previously returned exact attribute values are now returning longer, paraphrased responses (affects customers on mobile).
- Regression seems concentrated on the 32–80 token prompt range.

We attached a short PDF with before/after examples (acme_regression_samples.pdf). Can you: 1) confirm whether the v2.4 change could cause this; 2) advise whether we can pin or roll back to the prior model while you investigate? We’re in a pilot and need to avoid regression for our customers.

If possible, we’d like to pin to the prior version for the remainder of the pilot. Please let us know turnaround and impact on the pilot timeline.

Best,
Tom Briggs
Senior Product Manager | Acme Retail
Tom.Briggs@acme-retail.com

On Wed, Jul 1, 2026 at 14:02, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> [post-call recap]
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Tom Briggs <tom.briggs@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Diana Park <diana.park@acme-retail.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Jul 2026 09:00:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Sales discovery — model fit & next steps

Hi Tom — thanks for the quick note and for the examples. I’m sorry you hit that during the pilot. We take regressions very seriously.

Immediate plan (proposed)
1) Mitigate: We can pin your pilot to redwood-bert-2.3 (the prior verified production version) while we investigate the diff between v2.3 -> v2.4. Pinning is account-scoped and reversible; it will prevent further surprise changes during your evaluation.
2) Investigate: I’ve asked Product to run a targeted A/B evaluation on your prompt set (32–80 token bucket) and produce a diff report. Neha, Priyom — tagging you to evaluate risk and timeline.
3) Communicate: If you approve, I’ll schedule the pin/rollback window (small maintenance window with immediate cutover) and confirm timing.

Please confirm if you want us to proceed with pinning to redwood-bert-2.3 now. If yes, share any blackout windows where traffic change would be disruptive.

Attaching: eval_prompt_set_v1.jsonl (same set used in demo) and the Drive link for the benchmark runs.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

---
Attachment: eval_prompt_set_v1.jsonl
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com, priyom.das@redwood.com
Cc: Tom Briggs <tom.briggs@acme-retail.com>, Diana Park <diana.park@acme-retail.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Jul 2026 10:00:00 -0000
Subject: Fwd: ACME regression — request to pin/rollback to redwood-bert-2.3

Team — forwarding ACME thread. TL;DR: customer reports a quality regression after the v2.4 rollout affecting short extraction prompts. Customer requests pin to prior version for the pilot.

Ask / proposed owners
- Rishi (CS): own customer comms and confirm acceptance of proposed maintenance window.
- Neha (Product): run a focused diff on the attached prompt set (32–80 token bucket) and advise whether v2.4 behavior is intentional (model tuning) or a possible regression. Please include quantitative metrics (exact-match, F1, latency) and a brief summary.
- Priyom (SRE/Platform): if Product advises rollback/pin is required, can you schedule the account-scoped pin and provide rollback runbook + expected downtime? Also list any infra implications (caching, KV cache warmup).

Customer contact: Tom Briggs / Diana Park (see thread below). They’ve attached a small sample PDF; I’ve attached the prompt set we used in the demo. Time sensitivity: high — pilot is live and customer wants to avoid further customer-visible regressions.

Thanks — Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Briggs <tom.briggs@acme-retail.com>, Diana Park <diana.park@acme-retail.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Jul 2026 08:30:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Fwd: ACME regression — request to pin/rollback to redwood-bert-2.3

All — quick status update: we executed an account-scoped pin for Acme Retail at 08:12 UTC and rolled the default model for that account back to redwood-bert-2.3.

Details
- Action: pin account to redwood-bert-2.3 (version id: rb-2.3.0)
- Time: 2026-07-03 08:12:03 UTC
- Impact: negligible latency impact; no infra changes required beyond model routing config. KV cache will warm within ~10 minutes for typical traffic patterns.
- Validation: ran the quick-regression check against the provided prompt set; summary attached and full results uploaded to: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-acme-benchmarks (folder: /regression-checks/acme/2026-07-03). JIRA ticket SUP-4521 created to track deeper investigation.

Next steps
- Neha: please follow up with a short diff report (metrics + observations) by EOD so we can share a formal RCA with the customer.
- Rishi: please coordinate a quick sync with Tom (20 min) to confirm customer is back to expected behavior and agree whether we keep the pin for the remainder of the pilot.

Tom/Diana — apologies again for the disruption. Please let us know if you see any further odd outputs; we’ll keep monitoring and will share the full diff report once Neha’s done.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
SRE | Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.com
